findings.text: the successor-edge postcondition reads RETURN relationship.receipt_id, count(relationship), which Cypher groups by receipt_id, so when a derived HAS_SUCCESSOR edge (receipt_id null) coexists with the signed one the result is two rows of count 1 and successor_edge[0] picks whichever comes first; the exactly-one-edge the commit claims is therefore not enforced against a derived twin, and only duplicates sharing the signed receipt id are caught. The done-when's absent-edge case is still refused deterministically because an empty MATCH yields an empty result.

the fragment cites the negative-control log as negative_control.log, but the retained log is logs/negative-control-edge-write-removed.log, so the citation resolves to no file and a reader cannot open the red run the fragment points at.

baseline_suite and after_suite record their command with the angle-bracket placeholder <19 SN files: tests/standard_names/test_*.py from gate_files.txt> instead of the literal command that ran, so the recorded gate cannot be re-run as written; the explicit file list survives only in the base log header and the after log's summary line (168 passed, EXIT=0) is the operative evidence.
